questions.prompt: In a zero-based array of n elements stored contiguously, what is the worst-case number of elements shifted to insert a new item at index 0 when capacity is available?
questions.explanation: Every existing element must move one position right to open index zero, so n elements are shifted in the worst case.

questions.prompt: Why does direct access to A[i] in a contiguous array take constant time under the usual RAM model?
options: Its address is computed from the base address and i times the element size
The array is searched sequentially until index i
The element is copied to the beginning first
The array stores a linked pointer for each index
answer: Its address is computed from the base address and i times the element size
questions.explanation: The address calculation is base+i*element_size and takes constant arithmetic operations, independent of the array length.

questions.prompt: A row-major matrix has 12 columns and elements of 4 bytes. What is the byte offset of element A[7][5] from A[0][0], using zero-based indices?
questions.explanation: The linear index is 7*12+5=89. Multiplying by four bytes per element gives an offset of 356 bytes.

questions.prompt: For an R by C row-major matrix with zero-based indices, which formula gives the linear element index of A[i][j]?
questions.explanation: Each preceding row contributes C elements, then j elements in the current row, giving i*C+j.

questions.prompt: A C matrix A has row-major layout. Which loop order accesses a[i][j] with good spatial locality in the inner loop?
questions.explanation: In row-major storage, consecutive columns within a row are adjacent in memory. Keeping j in the inner loop walks contiguous elements and uses cache lines effectively.

questions.prompt: A row-major three-dimensional array B[2][3][4] is flattened to one-based element positions. What is the one-based position of B[1][2][3] using zero-based subscripts?
questions.explanation: The zero-based linear index is ((1*3)+2)*4+3=23. Converting to a one-based position gives 24.

questions.prompt: How many bytes are required for a row-major 4 by 7 integer matrix when each integer occupies 4 bytes and no extra padding is stored between elements?
questions.explanation: The matrix contains 4*7=28 integer elements. At four bytes each, the storage is 28*4=112 bytes.

questions.prompt: An array of n elements must be left-rotated by k positions in place using the reversal method. Which sequence performs the rotation with O(1) extra space?
answer: Reverse [0,k-1], reverse [k,n-1], then reverse the whole array
questions.explanation: Reversing each partition and then the full array restores the order within both blocks while moving the first k items to the end. It uses constant auxiliary storage and linear time.
options: Reverse [0,k-1], reverse [k,n-1], then reverse the whole array
Sort the array, then reverse it
Shift every element left k times using a temporary array of size n

questions.prompt: For a sorted array of n elements, what is the worst-case number of comparisons for binary search?
questions.explanation: Each comparison discards approximately half the remaining interval, so the number of levels grows logarithmically.

questions.prompt: Which statements about searching an unsorted array of n values are correct?
options: An absent key may require examining all n entries
A linear scan has worst-case time Theta(n)
Binary search is correct without any ordering or preprocessing
A scan has worst-case time O(log n)
answer: An absent key may require examining all n entries
A linear scan has worst-case time Theta(n)
questions.explanation: When the key is absent, a scan cannot stop early and must inspect every item. Without order or preprocessing, binary search cannot safely discard a half.

questions.prompt: An array-based list with spare capacity inserts an element at index k. Which expression best describes the number of elements shifted in the worst case?
questions.explanation: Elements at indices k through n-1 shift right, which is n-k items. Inserting at the end requires no shifts.

questions.prompt: Which statements about deleting an item from a packed array while preserving order are correct?
options: Deleting index k shifts n-k-1 later entries left
Deleting the last entry requires no suffix shift
Deleting any index always takes O(1) time
Compaction can preserve the relative order of remaining entries
answer: Deleting index k shifts n-k-1 later entries left
Deleting the last entry requires no suffix shift
Compaction can preserve the relative order of remaining entries
questions.explanation: All items after k move left to fill the gap, except when k is last. This compaction preserves the order but can take linear time.

questions.prompt: A dynamic array doubles capacity whenever it is full. Which statements about appending are correct?
options: An individual resizing append can take Theta(n) time
Append has amortized O(1) time over a sequence of operations
The total number of copied elements over m appends is O(m)
Every append has worst-case O(1) time
answer: An individual resizing append can take Theta(n) time
Append has amortized O(1) time over a sequence of operations
The total number of copied elements over m appends is O(m)
questions.explanation: A resize copies the current array, causing a linear worst-case operation. Geometric growth makes the total copies linear over many appends, yielding constant amortized cost.

questions.prompt: An initially empty dynamic array doubles capacity from 1 whenever full. After 9 appends, what is its capacity?
questions.explanation: The capacities after growth are 1, 2, 4, 8, and 16. The ninth item requires growth from 8 to 16.

questions.prompt: Which statements about contiguous arrays are correct?
options: They support constant-time indexed access under the RAM model
Inserting at the front can require shifting all existing elements
Every middle insertion is constant time
Their elements are individually allocated as linked nodes
answer: They support constant-time indexed access under the RAM model
Inserting at the front can require shifting all existing elements
questions.explanation: Indexing is calculated arithmetically from the base. Opening space near the front shifts later entries, while array elements are contiguous rather than separate linked nodes.

questions.prompt: A prefix-sum array P is defined by P[0]=0 and P[i+1]=P[i]+A[i]. How many array accesses are needed to answer a range-sum query A[l..r] after preprocessing?
options: Two prefix accesses and one subtraction
One access per array element in A
Theta(log n) accesses using binary search
answer: Two prefix accesses and one subtraction
questions.explanation: The range sum is P[r+1]-P[l], so two prefix values and one subtraction answer each query in constant time.

questions.prompt: For A=[3,-2,5,1,-4], define P[0]=0 and P[i+1]=P[i]+A[i]. What is the sum of A[1..3]?
An array A of length n is rotated left by k positions, where 0<=k<n. Which original index becomes the first element?
questions.explanation: A left rotation by k moves the original element at index k to index zero.

questions.prompt: An in-place reversal algorithm swaps symmetric elements until the indices meet. How many swaps are required for an array of length n?
questions.explanation: Each swap handles two elements, so exactly floor(n/2) symmetric pairs are exchanged.

questions.prompt: A loop executes for i=0; i<n; i+=3. How many iterations occur for positive n?
questions.explanation: The visited indices are 0,3,6,... strictly below n. Their count is the ceiling of n divided by 3.

questions.prompt: A nested loop runs for i=1..20 and j=1..i, inclusive. How many total inner iterations occur?
questions.explanation: The total is 1+2+...+20=20*21/2=210 iterations.

questions.prompt: A loop uses i=1; while (i<n) i*=2. What is its time complexity as a function of n?
questions.explanation: The loop variable doubles each iteration, so it reaches n after logarithmically many iterations.

questions.prompt: Which operations on a fixed-size contiguous array can require worst-case Theta(n) work?
options: Searching an unsorted array for an absent key
Inserting at index zero while shifting elements
Deleting at index zero while preserving order
Reading an element at a known index
answer: Searching an unsorted array for an absent key
Inserting at index zero while shifting elements
Deleting at index zero while preserving order
questions.explanation: An absent-key scan inspects all values. Front insertion and ordered deletion shift a linear number of entries; known-index access is constant time.

questions.prompt: A matrix A has 4 rows and 7 columns in row-major storage. How many elements precede A[3][2]?
questions.explanation: There are 3 complete rows before row 3, contributing 21 elements, plus two elements before column 2 in that row: 23.

questions.prompt: For a nonnegative array, a sliding window is used to find the longest subarray whose sum is at most K. Why can the left endpoint move only forward when the current sum exceeds K?
options: Removing elements from the left cannot increase the sum
The array is sorted by value
The sum is always unchanged by removal
The right endpoint must move backward
answer: Removing elements from the left cannot increase the sum
questions.explanation: With nonnegative entries, removing the leftmost element cannot increase the window sum. Therefore advancing the left endpoint restores feasibility without revisiting earlier positions.

questions.prompt: A two-pointer method searches for a pair summing to X in a sorted increasing array. If the current sum is too small, which pointer moves?
options: The smaller value is replaced by X
questions.explanation: Moving the left pointer to a larger value is the only direction that can increase the sum while preserving the candidate order.

questions.prompt: Two sorted arrays of lengths m and n are merged into one sorted array by the standard two-pointer procedure. What is the worst-case time?
questions.explanation: Each input element is copied once, so the total work is linear in the combined lengths.

questions.prompt: A sorted array [1,2,2,2,5,5,8] is compacted in place to unique values while preserving order. How many elements remain?
questions.explanation: The distinct values are 1, 2, 5, and 8. Stable compaction retains one occurrence of each, leaving four elements.

questions.prompt: In stable in-place compaction of a sorted array, what invariant does a write index typically maintain?
options: The prefix before it contains exactly the unique values seen so far
It always equals the current read index squared
It marks the smallest unseen value
It stores the number of duplicate pairs in the suffix
answer: The prefix before it contains exactly the unique values seen so far
questions.explanation: After processing a prefix, the write region contains the unique elements from that prefix in original sorted order.

questions.prompt: For an array A of length n, what is the worst-case number of comparisons needed to find its maximum by a single scan?
questions.explanation: The first element initializes the maximum. Each of the remaining n-1 elements is compared once against the current maximum.

questions.prompt: What is the worst-case number of comparisons required to find both minimum and maximum using the simple independent-scan approach?
questions.explanation: One scan performs n-1 comparisons for the maximum and another n-1 for the minimum, totaling 2n-2. Pairwise methods can improve this bound.

questions.prompt: Why can pairwise min-max scanning use fewer comparisons than two independent scans?
options: Each pair is first compared internally, then its smaller and larger values update separate extrema
It sorts the whole array first
It relies on the array being sorted
answer: Each pair is first compared internally, then its smaller and larger values update separate extrema
questions.explanation: For each pair, one comparison identifies a local low and high; only these candidates are compared with the global minimum and maximum.

questions.prompt: Kadane's algorithm for maximum subarray sum maintains a current ending sum. What update is applied at each element x?
questions.explanation: The best subarray ending here either starts at x or extends the prior ending subarray. Taking the maximum handles negative accumulated sums.

questions.prompt: For A=[-3,4,-1,2,-6,5], what is the maximum contiguous subarray sum?
questions.explanation: The subarray [4,-1,2] sums to 5. The final singleton 5 also gives 5, and no other contiguous segment is larger.

questions.prompt: An array of n integers is scanned once while maintaining a running sum and the best sum seen. What is the auxiliary space usage?
questions.explanation: Only a fixed number of scalar variables are maintained, so extra storage is constant with respect to n.

questions.prompt: An array has a length n and an element is accessed by a known index. Which property is required for the usual O(1) access bound?
options: The elements are stored contiguously with known element size
The array length is a power of two
answer: The elements are stored contiguously with known element size
questions.explanation: Contiguous storage lets the address be calculated from the base and index without traversing preceding elements.

questions.prompt: A circular buffer of capacity C maps a logical index i to a physical array slot. Which common mapping handles wraparound?
questions.explanation: Modulo capacity wraps indices back to the beginning of the backing array when they reach its end.

questions.prompt: A circular buffer has capacity 11 and head index 8. After advancing the head by 7 positions, what is its new physical index?
questions.explanation: The wrapped index is (8+7) mod 11=15 mod 11=4.

questions.prompt: A sorted array is rotated at an unknown pivot. Which property can support logarithmic search for a key?
options: At least one of the two halves around the midpoint is sorted
The minimum element is always at index zero
The array must contain no duplicates in every variant
answer: At least one of the two halves around the midpoint is sorted
questions.explanation: A midpoint divides the array so at least one side remains sorted, allowing elimination of a half based on the key range. Duplicates can complicate progress.

questions.prompt: In an array with all distinct elements, how many comparisons are sufficient to find a peak using binary search on the slope between adjacent entries?
questions.explanation: Comparing adjacent values indicates a direction containing a peak. Repeatedly discarding half the range gives logarithmic search.

questions.prompt: A difference array D represents range additions to A. To add x to every A[l..r], what two updates are made when a sentinel slot exists?
options: Add x to every D index in [l,r]
questions.explanation: The prefix sum of D reconstructs A. Starting an addition at l and canceling it after r uses +x at l and -x at r+1.

questions.prompt: A difference array receives +5 on range [2,6] and -3 on range [4,8]. What net addition applies at index 5?
questions.explanation: Index 5 lies in both ranges. Its net change is +5-3=+2.

questions.prompt: For an array A, let P[i] be the sum of elements before index i. Which formula gives the sum on half-open interval [l,r)?
questions.explanation: The prefix through positions before r minus the prefix before l leaves exactly A[l] through A[r-1].

questions.prompt: For a two-dimensional prefix-sum table P, which combination gives the sum of rectangle rows r1..r2 and columns c1..c2, inclusive?
questions.explanation: Subtract the strips above and left of the rectangle, then add back their overlap once. This inclusion-exclusion formula gives the rectangle sum.

questions.prompt: After O(RC) preprocessing of a two-dimensional prefix-sum table, what is the query time for one axis-aligned rectangle sum?
questions.explanation: Four table values and a constant number of additions/subtractions return the rectangle sum, independent of its area.

questions.prompt: What is the standard time complexity of multiplying two dense n by n matrices using the classical triple loop?
questions.explanation: There are n^2 output cells and each accumulates n products, producing n^3 arithmetic operations.

questions.prompt: For matrix multiplication C[i][j]+=A[i][k]*B[k][j] in row-major storage, which loop order gives contiguous access to B in the innermost loop?
options: i outer, k middle, j inner
i outer, j middle, k inner
j outer, i middle, k inner
k outer, j middle, i inner
answer: i outer, k middle, j inner
questions.explanation: With j innermost, B[k][j] and C[i][j] advance across adjacent columns, improving spatial locality in row-major layouts.

questions.prompt: Which statements about transposing a square matrix in place are correct?
options: Each off-diagonal pair A[i][j], A[j][i] is swapped once
Diagonal entries remain in their original positions
Restricting swaps to i<j avoids processing each pair twice
Every matrix entry must be moved into a temporary array
answer: Each off-diagonal pair A[i][j], A[j][i] is swapped once
Diagonal entries remain in their original positions
Restricting swaps to i<j avoids processing each pair twice
questions.explanation: The transpose exchanges symmetric off-diagonal cells. Diagonal cells are unchanged, and iterating over one triangle swaps each pair exactly once.

questions.prompt: A sorted array contains duplicate keys. What is the worst-case time to find the first occurrence with a modified binary search?
questions.explanation: After finding an equal value the search continues left, halving the remaining interval until the boundary is identified.

questions.prompt: To count occurrences of x in a sorted array with duplicates in O(log n), what should be found?
options: The first index of x and the first index greater than x
One occurrence and then a full scan
The minimum and maximum array values
The insertion position of every distinct key
answer: The first index of x and the first index greater than x
questions.explanation: Two binary searches find the half-open interval of x values. Subtracting the boundary indices gives the count.

questions.prompt: In a sorted array, the first occurrence of 6 is at index 4 and the first element greater than 6 is at index 11. How many occurrences of 6 are present?
questions.explanation: The matching entries occupy indices 4 through 10, so the half-open range length is 11-4=7.

questions.prompt: A fixed-width window of length k slides one position. After its first sum is known, what constant-time update advances it?
options: Subtract the outgoing value and add the incoming value
Recompute all k values and divide by k
Multiply the prior sum by k
answer: Subtract the outgoing value and add the incoming value
questions.explanation: Removing the leaving element and adding the entering element updates the sum in O(1), rather than scanning the entire window.

questions.prompt: For A=[4,-1,2,10,3], what is the largest sum among contiguous subarrays of length exactly 3?
questions.explanation: The three window sums are 5, 11, and 15. The last window [2,10,3] yields 15.

questions.prompt: Why does a sliding-window greedy method for sum-at-most-K constraints generally fail with negative array elements?
options: Removing a negative left element can increase the window sum
Negative values make array indexing invalid
Prefix sums cannot represent negative values
answer: Removing a negative left element can increase the window sum
questions.explanation: With negatives the sum is not monotone under removal: discarding a negative element can raise it, so the usual feasibility argument breaks.

questions.prompt: An equilibrium index i has equal sums strictly to its left and right. Given total sum and a running left sum, what is the time to find one?
questions.explanation: At each index, the right sum is total-left-A[i]. One pass updates the left sum and checks equality.

questions.prompt: For A=[2,-1,4,3,-2], what is an equilibrium index using zero-based indexing, if one exists?
questions.explanation: At index 2, the left sum is 2-1=1 and the right sum is 3-2=1.

questions.prompt: A two-dimensional prefix table stores sums over top-left rectangles. How many table entries are needed to answer one arbitrary rectangle-sum query?
questions.explanation: Inclusion-exclusion uses the prefix values at the lower-right, above, left, and overlapping corner positions.

questions.prompt: A sparse n by n matrix is stored as one (row,column,value) triple per nonzero. Ignoring metadata, when is this smaller in scalar slots than dense storage?
questions.explanation: Dense storage uses n^2 scalar values; triplet storage uses about 3z scalars. It is smaller under this model when 3z<n^2.

questions.prompt: A loop executes for i=1; i<=64; i*=2. How many body executions occur?
questions.explanation: The values are 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, and 64: seven executions.

questions.prompt: Two separate loops each run n iterations with constant work per iteration. What is their combined asymptotic time?
questions.explanation: Their costs add to n+n=2n, which is Theta(n). Sequential loops are not multiplied as nested loops are.

questions.prompt: A single pass stably compacts retained array items in place, reading each item once and writing each retained item once. What is the running time?
questions.explanation: There is constant work for each of the n input entries, so the total is linear.

questions.prompt: A permutation on n positions has k disjoint cycles including fixed points. How many swaps suffice to realize it?
questions.explanation: A cycle of length l requires l-1 swaps. Summing over cycle lengths gives n-k swaps.

questions.prompt: A permutation of 8 positions has nontrivial cycle lengths 3 and 2; the remaining positions are fixed. How many swaps suffice?
questions.explanation: There are five cycles total: lengths 3, 2, 1, 1, 1. The minimum swap count is 8-5=3.

questions.prompt: An array has distinct values from 1 through n except for one missing value. Which calculation recovers the missing value?
options: The array product divided by n
The array length squared minus its sum
questions.explanation: The expected sum of 1 through n is n(n+1)/2; subtracting the observed sum leaves the missing value.

questions.prompt: The values 1 through 8 appear in an array except one value; the array sum is 33. What is missing?
questions.explanation: The complete sum is 8*9/2=36. The absent value is 36-33=3.

questions.prompt: How much work is needed to sum the main diagonal of a square n by n matrix?
questions.explanation: The algorithm visits the n diagonal cells exactly once and performs constant work at each.

questions.prompt: In a naive row-major matrix transpose, what is the primary locality issue?
options: One of the read or write traversals may stride through noncontiguous memory
The output contains twice as many values
Every element changes its numeric value
The matrix cannot be traversed by columns
answer: One of the read or write traversals may stride through noncontiguous memory
questions.explanation: A row-major layout places columns far apart by row width. A transpose often reads or writes one side with a stride, reducing spatial locality.

questions.prompt: Which statements about array prefix-sum techniques are correct?
options: A 1-D prefix table answers static range sums in O(1) after O(n) preprocessing
A 2-D prefix table answers rectangle sums using four table values
A prefix table alone supports arbitrary range updates in O(1)
A range query must visit every element in the range
answer: A 1-D prefix table answers static range sums in O(1) after O(n) preprocessing
A 2-D prefix table answers rectangle sums using four table values
questions.explanation: Prefix tables answer static sums by subtracting boundary sums; two-dimensional inclusion-exclusion uses four entries. Updates may require rebuilding or a different data structure.

questions.prompt: A strictly increasing array is rotated at an unknown pivot. Why can binary search discard one half when looking for a key?
options: At least one half is sorted and its value range can be checked
The pivot is always the midpoint
The minimum remains at index zero
answer: At least one half is sorted and its value range can be checked
questions.explanation: With distinct values, one side of the midpoint is sorted. Comparing the key with that side's endpoints reveals whether it can lie there.

questions.prompt: A sorted array search returns the first index whose value is at least x, or n if none exists. What is that position called?
options: The count of values greater than x
questions.explanation: The lower bound divides values less than x from those at least x, giving the insertion position that preserves sorted order.

questions.prompt: A merge-based algorithm counts inversions while sorting an array. What is its running time?
questions.explanation: It divides the input recursively and counts cross-inversions during linear merges, yielding logarithmic levels of linear work.

questions.prompt: In a sorted-array pair-sum search, the current endpoint values sum to more than X. Which pointer moves?
questions.explanation: Decreasing the larger endpoint is the move that can lower the sum while retaining every potentially valid pair.

questions.prompt: With randomized pivots, what is the expected time of quickselect for finding the kth smallest item?
questions.explanation: Expected partition sizes shrink geometrically, so total work is linear, though a poor sequence of pivots can take quadratic time.

questions.prompt: If quickselect repeatedly partitions an n-item array into sizes 0 and n-1, what is its worst-case running time?
questions.explanation: The work sums n+(n-1)+...+1 when each partition removes only one element, producing a quadratic sum.

questions.prompt: For i=0..n-1, an inner loop runs j=i..n-1. How many inner iterations occur in total?
questions.explanation: The counts are n,n-1,...,1. Their sum is n(n+1)/2.

questions.prompt: An outer loop doubles its index each pass and an inner loop scans n elements. What is total time?
questions.explanation: There are logarithmically many outer iterations and each inner scan costs linear time.

questions.prompt: For dense matrices A(m by n) and B(n by p), what is the classical multiplication time?
questions.explanation: There are m*p output cells and each accumulates n products, for m*n*p arithmetic operations.

questions.prompt: Let A have dimensions m by n and B have dimensions n by p. Which statements about their classical matrix product are correct?
options: A*B is defined and has dimensions m by p
The classical algorithm takes Theta(mnp) arithmetic operations
The product is defined only when m=p
answer: A*B is defined and has dimensions m by p
The classical algorithm takes Theta(mnp) arithmetic operations
questions.explanation: The shared inner dimension n makes the product valid. It has m rows and p columns; each of its m*p entries uses n multiply-add terms.

questions.prompt: What are the dimensions of the transpose of an R by C matrix?
questions.explanation: Transposition exchanges rows and columns, so R rows and C columns become C rows and R columns.

questions.prompt: In row-major storage, which pair of entries in the same row is adjacent in memory?
questions.explanation: A row is stored contiguously, so neighboring column positions are consecutive elements in memory.

questions.prompt: In a row-major matrix with C columns and element size s bytes, what is the byte stride between A[i][j] and A[i+1][j]?
questions.explanation: Moving down one row advances C elements. Multiplying the row width by the element size gives a stride of C*s bytes.

questions.prompt: Why must a product-except-self algorithm handle zeros separately if it uses total-product division?
options: Division by a product containing zero is invalid
answer: Division by a product containing zero is invalid
questions.explanation: If any element is zero, the total product is zero and division cannot recover each position. Counting zeros or using prefix/suffix products avoids this issue.

questions.prompt: An array contains n+1 values drawn from 1..n and has at least one repeated value. Which statements are correct?
options: A duplicate is guaranteed by the pigeonhole principle
A functional graph can be formed by mapping each index to the value stored there
Floyd cycle detection can find a duplicate with O(1) extra space under the stated constraints
A hash set requires O(1) total space for arbitrary n
answer: A duplicate is guaranteed by the pigeonhole principle
A functional graph can be formed by mapping each index to the value stored there
Floyd cycle detection can find a duplicate with O(1) extra space under the stated constraints
questions.explanation: There are more entries than possible values, so a duplicate exists. The value mapping creates a cycle structure; Floyd detects it without a growing auxiliary set.

questions.prompt: An array of n elements is reversed in place by swapping symmetric pairs. Which statements are correct?
options: The number of swaps is floor(n/2)
A temporary array of length n is necessary
answer: The number of swaps is floor(n/2)
questions.explanation: Each symmetric pair is swapped once, producing floor(n/2) swaps and linear time. A temporary scalar is sufficient, so auxiliary space is constant.

questions.prompt: How many nonempty contiguous subarrays does an array of length 12 have?
questions.explanation: There are n(n+1)/2 choices of start and end with start<=end: 12*13/2=78.

questions.prompt: For an array of n elements, how many contiguous subarrays have length exactly k, where 1<=k<=n?
questions.explanation: The starting index ranges from 0 through n-k, giving n-k+1 possible windows.

questions.prompt: An array has length 20. How many contiguous subarrays have length exactly 6?
questions.explanation: The possible starting positions are 0 through 14, so the count is 20-6+1=15.

questions.prompt: How many unordered index pairs (i,j) with i<j exist in an array of n elements?
questions.explanation: Choose two distinct indices without ordering; the count is n choose 2.

questions.prompt: How many unordered pairs of distinct indices are there in an array of length 15?
questions.explanation: An array of length 15 has 15*14/2=105 unordered pairs of distinct indices. Each pair corresponds to one choice of two different positions.

questions.prompt: A sequence is queried frequently by random index and rarely modified in the middle. Which representation is usually suitable?
questions.explanation: An array provides constant-time indexed access with low per-element overhead, matching frequent random reads and few middle updates.

questions.prompt: An ordered array maintains sorted order. What is the worst-case time to insert a new item while preserving that order?
questions.explanation: Binary search locates the insertion point quickly, but the suffix may require a linear number of moves.

questions.prompt: A stored prefix-sum array P is explicitly maintained. What is the worst-case time to update P after changing A[k]?
questions.explanation: Every later prefix includes A[k], so direct maintenance may require updating a linear suffix of P.

questions.prompt: Which formula gives the number of nonempty contiguous subarrays of an n-element array?
questions.explanation: Each subarray is determined by a start and end with start<=end; summing by start yields n+(n-1)+...+1.

questions.prompt: In a row-major matrix, which nested-loop order generally gives sequential accesses for the innermost loop?
questions.explanation: A row is contiguous in memory, so iterating columns in the inner loop accesses neighboring cells.

questions.prompt: How many element slots are needed for a dense R by C matrix representation?
questions.explanation: A dense matrix stores one value for every row-column pair, yielding R times C entries.

questions.prompt: Which statements about binary search on an array are correct?
options: The searched range must be ordered by the comparison relation
Each midpoint comparison can eliminate about half the remaining candidates
Its worst-case comparisons are Theta(log n)
It is correct on every unsorted array without preprocessing
answer: The searched range must be ordered by the comparison relation
Each midpoint comparison can eliminate about half the remaining candidates
Its worst-case comparisons are Theta(log n)
questions.explanation: Sorted order supports discarding a half based on a midpoint comparison. The remaining interval shrinks geometrically, giving logarithmic worst-case comparisons.

questions.prompt: A dynamic-array append triggers a resize and copies n existing elements. What is the time of that individual append?
questions.explanation: A resizing append can allocate a new block and copy all current entries, which is linear for that operation even though amortized append is constant.

questions.prompt: A stable partition groups elements by a predicate. What property does stable guarantee?
options: Relative order is preserved within each group
The algorithm uses O(1) extra space
answer: Relative order is preserved within each group
questions.explanation: Stability preserves the original order among elements assigned to each group; it does not sort within the groups.

questions.prompt: For a row-major matrix, what is the locality effect of traversing a column top-to-bottom?
options: The access stride is the row width, so locality is worse than row traversal
Every access is to an adjacent element
The traversal is impossible without transposing
The algorithm visits only diagonal entries
answer: The access stride is the row width, so locality is worse than row traversal
questions.explanation: A fixed-column traversal jumps by C elements between rows, unlike consecutive-column accesses within a row.
